title: Adjunction for the closed-site lift
statement:
The functor $v$ is left adjoint to $u$, with $uv$ canonically the identity,
for the functors of [def-exc-closed-site-lift].

proof.text:
Write $R(D)=D/ID$ and $H(\overline C)=H_A(\overline C)$. For $V=\operatorname{Spec}\overline C$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}D$, the functors of [def-exc-closed-site-lift] give $v(V)=\operatorname{Spec}H(\overline C)$ and $u(U)=\operatorname{Spec}R(D)$. The contravariant Hom correspondence of [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and the natural bijection of [lem-exc-closed-lift-adjunction] give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(v(V),U)=\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,H(\overline C))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{A/I}(R(D),\overline C)=\operatorname{Hom}_Z(V,u(U)).$$
The restriction to maps over the bases is exact: the triangle over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ commutes precisely when the ring map preserves the $A$-algebra structure, For $A/I$, the triangle over $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ commutes precisely when the ring map preserves the $A/I$-algebra structure. Naturality in both variables follows from the cited natural algebra bijection and functoriality of Spec. Thus this is the Hom bijection for $v\dashv u$.

proof.text: For completeness, let $\alpha:\mathrm{id}\to HR$ and $\beta:RH\to\mathrm{id}$ be the unit and counit of the algebra adjunction $R\dashv H$ in [lem-exc-closed-lift-adjunction]. By [def-exc-closed-site-lift] and contravariant functoriality in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], define the site unit at $V=\operatorname{Spec}\overline C$ as $\eta_V=\operatorname{Spec}\beta_{\overline C}:V\to uv(V)$ and its counit at $U=\operatorname{Spec}D$ as $\epsilon_U=\operatorname{Spec}\alpha_D:vu(U)\to U$. For a ring map $f:D\to D\prime$, naturality $HR(f)\circ\alpha_D=\alpha_{D\prime}\circ f$ gives, with $g=\operatorname{Spec}f:U\prime\to U$, the equation $g\circ\epsilon_{U\prime}=\epsilon_U\circ vu(g)$. For $h:\overline C\to\overline C\prime$, naturality $h\circ\beta_{\overline C}=\beta_{\overline C\prime}\circ RH(h)$ gives, with $k=\operatorname{Spec}h:V\prime\to V$, the equation $uv(k)\circ\eta_{V\prime}=\eta_V\circ k$. Thus both site transformations are natural. The ring identities $H(\beta_{\overline C})\circ\alpha_{H(\overline C)}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\beta_{R(D)}\circ R(\alpha_D)=\mathrm{id}$ give respectively $\epsilon_{v(V)}\circ v(\eta_V)=\mathrm{id}_{v(V)}$ and $u(\epsilon_U)\circ\eta_{u(U)}=\mathrm{id}_{u(U)}$ after applying Spec. These are exactly the two site triangle identities.

proof.text: Under the reduction-induced Hom bijection of [lem-exc-closed-lift-adjunction], the identity of $H(\overline C)$ maps to the specified reduction map $\beta_{\overline C}:H(\overline C)/IH(\overline C)\to\overline C$. This map is an isomorphism by [lem-exc-closed-lift-reduction]. Consequently its spectrum $\eta_V$ from step 2 is an isomorphism, with inverse the spectrum of $\beta_{\overline C}^{-1}$; the two composites are identities by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For $k:V\prime\to V$, the equation $uv(k)\circ\eta_{V\prime}=\eta_V\circ k$ implies $\eta_V^{-1}\circ uv(k)=k\circ\eta_{V\prime}^{-1}$ by composing on the left with $\eta_V^{-1}$ and on the right with $\eta_{V\prime}^{-1}$. These are exactly the naturality equations for the inverse. Hence $\eta:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal B_Z}\xrightarrow{\sim}uv$ is the asserted canonical identification, rather than a literal equality of chosen objects.
